FIB_PLUS	<p>6948_901b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #02703e;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #02703e;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #02703e;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6497;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0b6497;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6497;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #883c81;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #883c81;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #883c81;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehx, +++, ehx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3636;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d3636;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3636;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #02703e;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #02703e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #02703e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #574ab9;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #574ab9;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #574ab9;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bmp, +++, bmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>b232_1fb6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6c0f;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3e6c0f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6c0f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006881;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006881;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006881;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #883c81;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #883c81;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>facf_c694</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #865000;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #865000;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #865000;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d5c;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d5c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d5c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ab2;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2b5ab2;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. FIB_PLUS	<p>6eb9_c2b1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #865000;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #865000;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #865000;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #02703e;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #02703e;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #02703e;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ab2;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2b5ab2;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ab2;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dry, +++, dry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>8e41_d2ac</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6c0f;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3e6c0f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6c0f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6497;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0b6497;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6497;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #883c81;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #883c81;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #883c81;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahr, +++, ahr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>84ee_d4f3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #944214;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #944214;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #944214;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3e6c0f;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3e6c0f;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6c0f;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #574ab9;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #574ab9;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #574ab9;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fkm, +++, fkm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>5978_1208</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #755a00;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #755a00;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #755a00;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006881;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006881;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006881;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #883c81;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #883c81;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #883c81;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mnw, +++, mnw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>a96e_2287</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #865000;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #865000;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #865000;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006881;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006881;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006881;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #883c81;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #883c81;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #883c81;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, acd, +++, acd"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #616206;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #616206;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #616206;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006b6f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #574ab9;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #574ab9;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made.
